entry.en: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Nicaragua.
entry.es: Tu pasaporte debe tener una validez de al menos 6 meses después de la fecha de llegada a Nicaragua.
entry.quote: To enter Nicaragua, your passport must have an ‘expiry date’ at least 6 months after the date you arrive.

entry.en: You may be refused entry if you do not have an onward ticket.
entry.es: Podrían negarte la entrada si no tienes un boleto de salida.
entry.quote: You may be refused entry if you do not have an onward ticket.

entry.en: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.
entry.es: Se exige certificado de vacunación contra la fiebre amarilla si vienes de un país con riesgo de transmisión.
entry.quote: you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had a yellow fever vaccination if you’re coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

entry.en: Electronic cigarettes and similar devices are banned, and customs can confiscate them at the border.
entry.es: Los cigarrillos electrónicos y dispositivos similares están prohibidos y la aduana puede confiscarlos en la frontera.
entry.quote: You cannot import, export, sell, store or use these devices, with or without nicotine. Customs officials can confiscate these products at the border.

entry.en: You must pay an arrival tax of 10 US dollars in cash.
entry.es: Debes pagar una tasa de llegada de 10 dólares estadounidenses en efectivo.
entry.quote: You must pay an arrival tax of 10 US dollars in cash.

entry.en: A tourist card costs US$10 and is obtained on arrival with a passport valid for at least six months.
entry.es: La tarjeta de turista cuesta 10 USD y se obtiene a la llegada con un pasaporte válido por al menos seis meses.
entry.quote: Visitors must obtain a Tourist Card for US$10 valid for 1 month to 3 months (depending on citizenship - Canada and United States are allowed 90 days) upon arrival, provided with a valid passport with at least six months to run.

safety.en: It is illegal for foreigners to take part in any political activity, and they can be arrested, detained or deported.
safety.es: Es ilegal que los extranjeros participen en cualquier actividad política y pueden ser arrestados, detenidos o deportados.
safety.quote: It is illegal for foreigners to take part in any sort of political activity in Nicaragua. You can be arrested and detained or deported for:

safety.en: Criminals often attack people in vehicles, so keep car windows closed and doors locked.
safety.es: Los delincuentes suelen atacar a personas en vehículos, así que mantén las ventanillas cerradas y las puertas con seguro.
safety.quote: Criminals often carry out attacks on people in vehicles. To reduce the risk to yourself and your belongings:

safety.en: There is a risk of express kidnapping if you use an unauthorised taxi.
safety.es: Existe riesgo de secuestro exprés si usas un taxi no autorizado.
safety.quote: There is a risk of ‘express kidnapping’ if you use an unauthorised taxi.

safety.en: There are strong currents off sections of the Pacific coast, with no warning signs or lifeguards, and people have drowned.
safety.es: Hay fuertes corrientes en tramos de la costa del Pacífico, sin señales de advertencia ni salvavidas, y han muerto personas ahogadas.
safety.quote: There are strong currents off sections of Nicaragua’s Pacific coast and people have drowned. There are no warning signs or lifeguards

safety.en: Do not hike on volcanoes without an experienced guide.
safety.es: No hagas senderismo en volcanes sin un guía con experiencia.
safety.quote: Do not hike on volcanoes without an experienced guide.

safety.en: Driving standards are low and road conditions are generally poor, with no street lighting on main highways.
safety.es: El nivel de conducción es bajo y las carreteras suelen estar en mal estado, sin alumbrado en las carreteras principales.
safety.quote: Road conditions are generally poor. There is no street lighting on the main highways between major cities and only minimal street lighting in towns. Avoid driving at night.

health.en: Public hospitals are not well equipped, except for some in Managua, and private hospitals usually take payment up front in cash.
health.es: Los hospitales públicos están mal equipados, salvo algunos en Managua, y los privados suelen cobrar por adelantado en efectivo.
health.quote: Public hospitals in Nicaragua are not well equipped, except for some hospitals in Managua.

health.en: Health risks include malaria, dengue and Zika virus.
health.es: Los riesgos de salud incluyen malaria, dengue y virus del Zika.
health.quote: See what health risks you’ll face in Nicaragua, including:

health.en: Dengue is present in some areas, and malaria is not a serious concern unless you go to the Caribbean coast or along the Rio San Juan.
health.es: El dengue está presente en algunas zonas, y la malaria no es grave salvo en la costa caribeña o a lo largo del río San Juan.
health.quote: Dengue fever is present in some areas and comes from a type of mosquito that flies mostly between dusk and dawn. Malaria is not of serious concern unless you are heading to the Caribbean coast or along the Rio San Juan east of San Carlos.

health.en: Tap water in Managua is reportedly safe to drink, but chlorinated bottled water is always the best choice.
health.es: Según se indica, el agua del grifo en Managua es potable, pero el agua embotellada con cloro siempre es la mejor opción.
health.quote: the tap water in Managua is safe to drink, but bottled water with chlorine is always the best choice.

health.en: You cannot use British-issued prescriptions locally.
health.es: No puedes usar recetas emitidas en el Reino Unido en el país.
health.quote: You cannot use British-issued prescriptions locally.

help.en: The emergency number for ambulance, fire and police is 911.
help.es: El número de emergencias para ambulancia, bomberos y policía es el 911.

help.en: There is no resident British diplomatic mission in Nicaragua; emergency help comes from the British Embassy in San Jose, Costa Rica.
help.es: No hay misión diplomática británica residente en Nicaragua; la ayuda de emergencia viene de la Embajada Británica en San José, Costa Rica.
help.quote: There is no resident British diplomatic mission in Nicaragua, and FCDO cannot give in-person support. If you need emergency help or have passport-related issues, contact the British Embassy in San Jose, Costa Rica

getting_in.en: Most visitors fly into Augusto C Sandino airport in Managua (MGA).
getting_in.es: La mayoría de los visitantes llega al aeropuerto Augusto C. Sandino de Managua (MGA).
getting_in.quote: You will most likely fly into Augusto C Sandino airport in Managua (MGA IATA).

getting_in.en: Flying into Liberia (LIR) or San José (SJO) in Costa Rica can make sense for some destinations, with immigration at the airport and again entering Nicaragua.
getting_in.es: Volar a Liberia (LIR) o San José (SJO) en Costa Rica puede convenir para algunos destinos, con migración en el aeropuerto y de nuevo al entrar a Nicaragua.
getting_in.quote: it may make sense to fly to Liberia LIR IATA or San José SJO IATA airport (which is in Alajuela) in Costa Rica instead. Costa Rica is not part of the CA4, and you will pass through immigration both at the airport and when entering Nicaragua.

getting_in.en: By land departure the exit tax is US$4, and it is not accepted in Nicaraguan córdobas.
getting_in.es: Al salir por tierra la tasa es de 4 USD y no se acepta en córdobas nicaragüenses.
getting_in.quote: By land departure the exit tax is US$4. Be aware that they do not accept the equivalent in Nicaraguan Cordobas (local currency).

getting_around.en: Bus is the main mode of travel, mostly old decommissioned yellow US school buses.
getting_around.es: El autobús es el principal medio de transporte, en su mayoría antiguos autobuses escolares amarillos de EE. UU.
getting_around.quote: Bus is definitely the main mode of travel in Nicaragua

getting_around.en: Most buses are old decommissioned yellow US school buses and are expected to be packed full.
getting_around.es: La mayoría de los autobuses son antiguos autobuses escolares amarillos de EE. UU. y se espera que vayan llenos.
getting_around.quote: Most of the buses are old decommissioned yellow  US school buses (though often fantastically repainted and redecorated). Expect these buses to be packed full

getting_around.en: A typical bus fare ranges from US$1 or less for short trips to US$3–4 for longer ones.
getting_around.es: Una tarifa típica de autobús va de 1 USD o menos en trayectos cortos a 3–4 USD en trayectos largos.
getting_around.quote: A typical fare may vary between US$1 or less for short (~30min) trips to US$3–4 for longer trips.

getting_around.en: Microbuses are vans holding up to 15 people and cost a bit more than the school buses but are faster.
getting_around.es: Los microbuses son furgonetas para hasta 15 personas; cuestan algo más que los autobuses escolares pero son más rápidos.
getting_around.quote: The microbuses cost a little more than the school buses, but are faster, making fewer stops.

getting_around.en: You cannot drive or import right-hand-drive vehicles into Nicaragua.
getting_around.es: No se pueden conducir ni importar vehículos con volante a la derecha en Nicaragua.
getting_around.quote: You cannot drive or import right-hand-drive vehicles into Nicaragua.

money.en: The national currency is the córdoba oro (NIO), and most places also accept US dollars, sometimes at less than face value.
money.es: La moneda nacional es el córdoba oro (NIO) y la mayoría de los lugares acepta también dólares, a veces por debajo de su valor.
money.quote: The national currency is called the córdoba oro (ISO code NIO, locally abbreviated as C$)

money.en: Córdobas are essential for bus fares, taxis and small meals, so carry around C$500 in small bills.
money.es: Los córdobas son esenciales para autobuses, taxis y comidas pequeñas; conviene llevar unos C$500 en billetes pequeños.
money.quote: Córdobas are essential when paying bus fares, taxis, small meals and other daily purchases; try to have somewhere around C$500 in small bills on you at all times.

money.en: Most ATMs use only the Visa/Plus system, and all give local currency.
money.es: La mayoría de los cajeros usa solo el sistema Visa/Plus y todos entregan moneda local.
money.quote: All ATMs give out local currency and most can dispense US dollars too.

money.en: US$100 and US$50 notes are often not accepted except by banks, so bring US$20 bills and small notes.
money.es: Los billetes de 100 y 50 USD a menudo no se aceptan salvo en bancos, así que conviene llevar billetes de 20 USD y de menor valor.
money.quote: US$100 and US$50 notes are often not accepted at all except by banks

money.en: Banks do not exchange British pounds; the US dollar is the only foreign currency freely exchangeable.
money.es: Los bancos no cambian libras esterlinas; el dólar estadounidense es la única divisa extranjera de cambio libre.
money.quote: The US dollar, either in cash or travellers cheques, is the only foreign currency freely exchangeable in Nicaragua. Banks do not exchange British pounds.

etiquette.en: Formal 'usted' is used with strangers, older people and higher-ranking people.
etiquette.es: Se usa el 'usted' formal con desconocidos, personas mayores y de mayor rango.
etiquette.quote: The formal form ("usted" for one person, "ustedes" for several people) is used with strangers, older people and higher-ranking people.

etiquette.en: Don and Doña before a given name are common polite forms of address.
etiquette.es: Don y Doña antes del nombre de pila son formas corteses de dirigirse a las personas.
etiquette.quote: Don (for men) and Doña (for women) are a common term to politely address people with their given name.

etiquette.en: Nicaraguans are very conscious about appearance and do not understand tourists who go around in shabby or unkempt clothes.
etiquette.es: Los nicaragüenses cuidan mucho su apariencia y no entienden que los turistas anden con ropa desaliñada.
etiquette.quote: Nicaraguans are very conscious about their appearance and don't understand why "rich" tourists would go around in shabby clothes or unkempt.

etiquette.en: Most people do not take well to their faith being ridiculed or to overt proselytizing.
etiquette.es: A la mayoría no le agrada que se ridiculice su fe ni el proselitismo abierto.
etiquette.quote: most people like their faith (usually Catholic) the way it is, thank you, and don't take too well to it being ridiculed or overt attempts at proselytizing.

etiquette.en: Women going topless at the beach is certainly a no-no.
etiquette.es: Que las mujeres hagan topless en la playa es definitivamente un tabú.
etiquette.quote: females going topless at the beach is certainly a no-no.

etiquette.en: Nicknames based on appearance, such as 'chele', are common and not considered offensive.
etiquette.es: Los apodos basados en la apariencia, como 'chele', son comunes y no se consideran ofensivos.
etiquette.quote: Nicknames such as "gorda" (fat lady), "flaco" (skinny man), or "negro" (black), are common and are not considered offensive.
